text: This is Cohort. An A.I. engineering team that runs on your own machine.
It starts with your team. A full roster of specialists: architect, frontend, backend, Q.A., code reviewer, security, and more. Each with its own role and system prompt. And you can add your own.
You send one message to the team lead. No tickets, no board. Just describe what you want built.
Here, a full personal finance app. Attach a brief, hit send, and that one sentence becomes the plan.
In seconds, the lead consults a product manager for acceptance criteria, turns it into an epic, and plans the work as parallel streams.
It's decomposed into stream-tagged tasks on a live board, with dependencies. Every specialist works in parallel, each in its own git worktree, so nothing ever collides.
And they don't work in a vacuum. These are grounded, persistent agents that brainstorm and align before writing a line of code.
Then it gets serious. The code reviewer catches a real floating-point bug and blocks the pull request.
And it's not just review. Every task must pass Q.A., security, and coverage.
When a check fails, the lead files it as a new work item and re-runs the gate. Nothing merges until it's green.
Once the bar is met, an independent reviewer signs off, and it's a real merge.
One dashboard keeps you in command. Epics, tokens, and who's active, at a glance.
From one sentence, to shipped, reviewed code. Powered by the GitHub Copilot S.D.K. This is Cohort. Your A.I. engineering team.
